clue.text: Arctic footwear is currently quiet on half of floe

parts.note: 's is the short form of is
currently means at present, now
sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word floe gives its back two letters here

explanation.surface: A remark about polar boots and the hush out on the ice floe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' becomes 'S and 'currently' NOW, so together they give SNOW; 'half of' takes the second half of floe, OE.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad racket-like frames strapped to boots spread a walker's weight on deep powder in polar regions.

clue.text: Beer? There's little new in mine

indicators.note: in places the small letter inside the word for a mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
N is the short form of new

explanation.surface: A miner asking whether there is a drink on offer down the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of ale in a British pub is ordered by that quantity, so the measure stands for the drink.

clue.text: Have a meal in attempt to achieve agreement

indicators.note: in tells us the eating goes inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: Diplomats sharing dinner in hope of reaching a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact between states is a signed accord.

clue.text: Graduate teacher takes on English, though an expert in ancient history

indicators.note: takes on means adds on at the end, so the letter follows

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree

explanation.surface: A newly qualified teacher picks up English classes despite being a classics specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was the eighth-century monk who wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was the early medieval monk-historian whose chronicle is the chief source for Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: In translation, I read a blue French poet

indicators.note: in translation suggests the words are put into another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reading a melancholy verse in English rendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In translation' rearranges the ten letters of I READ A BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire wrote Les Fleurs du mal, the nineteenth-century collection of verse.

clue.text: Staying sober in most of brawl shows firmness of character

indicators.note: in places the abstainer's letters inside the shortened brawl
most of drops the last letter of the word for a brawl

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl
TT means teetotal, staying sober

explanation.surface: Keeping off the drink in the thick of a fight shows strong character.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is the usual crossword way to say someone stays off alcohol; 'brawl' here is a confused free-for-all fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and resolve under pressure is a person's grit.

clue.text: PC in here disentangled code

indicators.note: disentangled suggests knotted letters being pulled apart and laid out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A computer in this room has untangled a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disentangled' rearranges the letters of PC IN HERE; 'code' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a message into cipher is to code it, both verbs.

clue.text: Instrument with which to damage working contemporary art venue

parts.note: to harm is to damage
on means working, as a machine is on
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: Someone describing a tool for vandalising a working modern gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA, the Institute of Contemporary Arts, is a London gallery on the Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a small reed wind instrument.

clue.text: English leading most of road race round? It could provide a good finish!

definitions.text: It could provide a good finish

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the letter goes in front
round means turned about, so the shortened race is read backwards
most of drops the last letter of the race's name

parts.note: Le Mans is the famous French 24-hour motor race on public roads

explanation.surface: An English driver in front for most of a motor race lap, with a good finish promised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts LE MANS to LEMAN, and 'round' turns that into NAMEL, with E in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard glossy paint or glaze gives a surface its shiny final coat.

clue.text: The gutless in conflict? Good running material!

indicators.note: in places the emptied word inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: gutless removes the insides of a word, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cowards in a war, and a remark about fabric that is good for jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutless' keeps only the outside letters of 'The'. The definition plays on 'running' as flowing, as from a tap, not jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid from a tap is the stuff that flows, as in running taps.

clue.text: Stake involving City-the same story

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the stake's letters go around the rest

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake
EC is the postcode area for the City of London
do, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: A gambling stake involving the City, and the same old tale.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City of London, and DO is short for ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing account of a real incident is a brief tale.

clue.text: Piece of music, sharp, loud, by Bernstein (last three parts only), possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words could be arranged otherwise, so their letters are rearranged
last three parts only keeps just the closing three letters of the conductor's name

explanation.surface: A piece of music, played sharp and loud, perhaps by Bernstein, though only its last three movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last three parts only' keeps EIN from Bernstein; 'possibly' rearranges those letters with SHARP, LOUD and BY. Leonard Bernstein famously played and recorded this Gershwin piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's 1924 work for piano and jazz band is a celebrated concert composition.

clue.text: Disparaging spinning record -Love scoundrel-in energetic dance

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the record's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: in places the love and the scoundrel inside the dance

parts.note: the jive is a lively dance
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A scathing review of a record about a love rat at a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' turns the record round; 'Love' is O because a zero score in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A belittling, derogatory word or remark is one that expresses contempt.

clue.text: Nobody not ninety is doddery?

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters totter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone under ninety yet already shaky, and so of no account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doddery' rearranges the letters of NOT NINETY.
explanation.definitionFit: An insignificant person with no importance is a nobody.

clue.text: Order a number to return, taking care of unfinished job

indicators.note: taking care of means holding and protecting, so the number's letters wrap round the rest
to return means to go back, so the number is read backwards

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the word job

explanation.surface: An instruction for a crowd to come back and look after a half-done task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To return' reads the number backwards, giving ENIN, and 'taking care of' wraps it round the unfinished job.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin is to command or instruct someone formally.

clue.text: French delicacy in tin is in a poor condition

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
something that ails is unwell or in poor shape

explanation.surface: A tinned French treat that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots, cooked in garlic butter, are a famous dish in France.

clue.text: Deciding student is involved in posing problems

indicators.note: is involved in places the learner's letter inside the setting

parts.note: setting problems means posing them, as an examiner does
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Settling matters while a student causes difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the learner plate, stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter is to resolve or decide it.

clue.text: Was now correct in variation form, absorbing a piece of film music

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the a goes inside the rearranged letters
in variation form suggests a theme played differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician tidying a theme into variations while taking in a film score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In variation form' rearranges WAS NOW CORRECT, and 'absorbing' takes in A. Richard Addinsell wrote it for the 1941 film Dangerous Moonlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Addinsell's short piano concerto was written for a wartime British film score.

clue.text: 1 added to 10 will make 24?

indicators.note: added to means slotted into, so the numeral goes inside the other entry

parts.note: 10 refers to the entry at 10 across, which the solver must already have
1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sum asking whether one plus ten makes twenty-four.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are cross-references: 10 is the answer at 10 across and 24 is the answer at 24 across, a word for someone who serves; 1 is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves at table in a restaurant is a server, the answer at 24 across.

clue.text: Stops design of squares

explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to check it, and a pattern of squares like gingham is a check pattern.

clue.text: Repugnance for leader of thieves intervening in endless calamity

indicators.note: intervening in means coming between, so the letter goes inside the shortened calamity
endless drops the last letter of the word for calamity

parts.note: a disaster is a calamity

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word thieves

explanation.surface: Disgust felt toward a gang boss caught up in some never-ending catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts DISASTER to DISASTE, and 'leader of' gives T to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong dislike or aversion is a feeling of revulsion.

clue.text: Choice of ends for service gets you aggrieved

indicators.note: of here means sitting between, so the choice word goes between the two ends
ends for takes the first and last letters of the word service

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: Picking which end to serve from in tennis, and feeling hard done by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends for' takes the first and last letters of service, S and E, with OR between.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling resentful or hurt is being upset at an injustice.

clue.text: Force one Member to rush, being taken short

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MBE

indicators.note: being taken short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to pelt is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: An MP forced to dash off when caught short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being taken short' cuts PELT to PEL; M stands for Member, as in MBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or compel someone to act is to push them into it.

clue.text: Attempt to make hole in 80% of soft material

indicators.note: 80% of a five-letter word keeps its first four letters, dropping the last

parts.note: putty is a soft pliable material

explanation.surface: Trying to make a hole in a mostly soft substance.
explanation.walkthrough: '80%' keeps four of the five letters of the soft material. The definition is golf: a gentle stroke on the green aimed at the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: On the golf green a gentle stroke aimed at the cup is the shot to sink the ball.

clue.text: Computer equipment runs during cut

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the letter goes inside the word for cut

parts.note: to sever is to cut
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Equipment running while a cable is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for runs, as on a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A networked machine that hosts files or websites for other computers is a key piece of IT hardware.

clue.text: Abode of hapless police (though showing style following clues)

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the style goes after the clues

parts.note: keys are clues or answers that unlock a puzzle
tone is manner or style

explanation.surface: A detective's note on where bungling officers live, with stylish clue-following.
explanation.walkthrough: The Keystone Cops were the bumbling police of silent film comedies, from the Keystone studio.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent-film studio gave its name to the bungling Kops, so it is their home.
